summary: The submission establishes a synthetic counterexample to inferring majority-vote benefit from individual accuracy alone. It does not establish actual AI performance or a result about ten unanimous reviewers. There were no existing findings or graph relations to reconcile. The operator labels this an end-to-end listener test, but the execution report records no executed checks.
open_questions: Which joint error patterns occur in the prespecified AI task family?
How do unanimous-answer selection and discussion affect accuracy, coverage and wrong-anchor susceptibility?
next_question: On at least 200 prespecified public or synthetic tasks, does a preregistered panel rule outperform the required cost-matched baselines on held-out tasks, with task-level paired uncertainty and no worsening of wrong-anchor susceptibility beyond the stated margin?

relations.reason: The majority-accuracy counterexample does not transfer directly to accuracy conditional on unanimous agreement.

findings.text: Both distributions give every reviewer accuracy 0.6. World A gives majority accuracy 0.6. World B is normalized because 0.4 + 3 × 0.2 = 1; each reviewer is correct with probability 0.4 + 0.2 = 0.6, while the majority is correct only with probability 0.4. Thus identical marginal accuracies can accompany unchanged or reduced majority accuracy.
findings.quote: Three reviewers can each have accuracy 0.6 while their majority has accuracy either 0.6 or 0.4, depending only on their joint error distribution.
findings.verification:
Verified nonnegativity, normalization, marginal accuracies and majority accuracies by mathematical reasoning from the stated outcomes. No code, simulation, panel experiment or trusted harness check was executed.
Execution ledger: No execution attributed to this finding; reasoning only.

findings.text: The counterexample concerns unconditional majority accuracy. For these binary constructions, unanimity occurs with probability 1 in world A and conditional accuracy 0.6; in world B it occurs with probability 0.4 and conditional accuracy 1. The construction therefore does not demonstrate reduced accuracy conditional on unanimous agreement.
findings.quote: They compare unconditional majority correctness; they do not assert that conditioning on unanimous agreement has the same probability in these worlds.
findings.verification:
Derived unanimity probabilities and conditional accuracies from the enumerated binary outcomes. No empirical agreement effects or proposed panel comparison were executed.
Execution ledger: No execution attributed to this finding; reasoning only.
